text:
lia-csr: Heads up — enterprise customer (acct: ACME) just reported a spike in function-call failures starting ~10:22 UTC after we began the v3.2 canary. They're seeing schema validation errors for a tool we call `order_lookup`.

ashley: Can you paste the error and a sample request/response? Also which rollout percentage is v3.2 on right now?

lia-csr: Error from their logs: `{"error":"schema validation failed","details":"missing required field 'order_id' in tool args"}`. They say the same request worked before the rollout. We had v3.2 at 15% traffic about 10:20 UTC (canary=15). Full logs below.

lia-csr: Customer sample request (sanitized):
```
POST /v1/chat/completions
{
  "model": "redwood-model-v3.2",
  "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"lookup order 12345"}],
  "functions": [{"name":"order_lookup","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"order_id":{"type":"string"}},"required":["order_id"]}}]
}
```

lia-csr: Response they got:
```
200 OK
{"id":"resp_abc","choices":[{"message":{"role":"assistant","content":null,"function_call":{"name":"order_lookup","arguments":"{\"id\":\"12345\"}"}}]} 
```

lia-csr: So the model returned `arguments` JSON with `id` instead of the required `order_id` key — schema validation rejects it downstream.

kevin: Interesting. That suggests v3.2 is choosing a different alias for the arg name. Could be model-level schema mapping/regression. Any traces/route ids we can use to find which runtime variant handled it?

lia-csr: Customer provided trace-id `trace-ACME-9982`. They say ~300 requests failed over 10:20–10:30 UTC window. Latency was normal, just schema mismatch. Billing spike? They noted retries causing extra tokens but haven't quantified.

priya: Pulling canary logs now. @deploy-bot can you confirm which kernel/serialization change went in with v3.2? I remember a tweak to function calling normalization.

deploy-bot: Deployment v3.2 pushed at 10:15 UTC. Change list: function-call normalization: alias-stripping fix, normalized param name mapping feature flag `fn_aliasing=v2` enabled by default for v3.2.

priya: That feature is suspect. On older model binary we had strict parameter names. v3.2 attempted to normalize arg names from natural language heuristics which can produce `id` instead of `order_id`.

jonah: Canary at 15% means many enterprise requests could hit it. We should decide fast: roll back canary to 0% or patch mapping. Risk: rollback will affect rollout metrics but stops customer impact.

ashley: Customer is on an enterprise SLA. Lia, what's their tolerance? They want a fix asap.

lia-csr: They're asking for immediate mitigation. They can accept a temporary routing override to pin them to v3.1.

kevin: Short-term mitigation: route ACME's traffic to v3.1 via routing policy. I can push a customer-specific rule if product approves. Long-term: revert fn_aliasing or update normalization mapping to preserve original parameter names.

priya: I can reproduce locally if I feed the same assistant completion prompt to v3.2 vs v3.1. Quick repro script attached:
```
# repro.sh
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-model-v3.2","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"lookup order 12345"}],"functions":[{"name":"order_lookup","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"order_id":{"type":"string"}},"required":["order_id"]}}]}'
```

priya: v3.2 returns `{"arguments":"{\"id\":\"12345\"}"}`; v3.1 returns `{"arguments":"{\"order_id\":\"12345\"}"}`.

jonah: OK let's do two things immediately: 1) kevin, apply a routing override for customer ACME to pin to v3.1; 2) priya, disable `fn_aliasing` in the v3.2 canary config (or revert) and re-run a small canary subset with tests.

kevin: On it. Pushing routing rule now. Will monitor for any failed requests. ETA ~3 mins.

kevin: Routing rule applied for acct ACME -> model=v3.1. Confirmed at 10:38 UTC. Lia: can you ask customer to retry a failing request and provide new trace ids?

lia-csr: Sent to customer; they're retrying. New trace `trace-ACME-9990`. They confirm success now, no schema errors.

ashley: Great. That proves the regression is model-specific. Priya, if fn_aliasing is the cause, what's the plan for a fix and timeline?

priya: Plan: rollback `fn_aliasing` feature flag in canary to `v1` (strict). I can push a config change to canary immediately and run regression tests against our function-calling test suite (1000 prompts). If all green, we can re-enable with better mapping rules. Timeline: change + test run ~30–45 minutes. If test shows further regressions we'll rollback binary.

jonah: Make that a priority. Also add an automated guard in rollout pipeline to run schema-preservation smoke tests for function-calling models.

ashley: I'll log a P1 support ticket referencing trace ids and steps taken for the customer record and legal/compliance.

lia-csr: Customer is satisfied with the pinning. They asked if we can proactively scan other enterprise customers who use `order_lookup`-style tools. Suggestion: run a quick query to find customers with function signatures that include `order_id` or similar.

kevin: I'll add an ad-hoc query over routing logs to find top impacted contracts and inform CS.

priya: Follow-up: after I disable fn_aliasing on canary I'll run the repro script and post results here. If any odd edge cases appear we might need a patch to the normalization code.

deploy-bot: Config change `fn_aliasing=v1` applied to canary group at 10:52 UTC (by priya). Running test suite (id: fs-2026-04).

priya: Tests running — currently 0/1000 failures after change. Will update after full run.

ashley: Noted. Lia: keep ACME ticket open until we've got a full postmortem and change logged.

lia-csr: Will do. Also capturing customer-impact numbers and potential billing adjustments for retry churn.

kevin: After action items: 1) pin ACME -> v3.1 (done), 2) revert fn_aliasing on canary (done), 3) add function-call schema smoke test to rollout pipeline (jonah/priya), 4) follow-up customer compensation eval (support/finance).

priya: I'll prepare a short postmortem draft once tests complete. Preliminary cause: over-aggressive arg-name normalization in v3.2 led to semantic key renaming causing downstream schema validation failures in tool invocation.

lia-csr: Customer thanked us and asked to be notified before future model rollouts. We offered a pre-rollout notification and a client pinning option.

ashley: Nice recovery. Keep updates here and we'll convert into formal incident doc after tests.

lia-csr: Closing loop for now — will update when postmortem ready. :white_check_mark:
